Coach's note, Tuesday — Pooja, under-16 hockey
Pooja came to practice today with a sheet of paper folded in her pocket. She has a Chemistry test on Friday and our district match on Saturday, and last week she looked exhausted. I asked how she was managing. She unfolded the sheet: two columns she had labelled "due soon" and "matters long term". Test revision: both. Saturday's match: both. Her evening online game with her cousins: neither, she said, "just habit". So she has dropped the gaming this week, not practice. She explained it to me like a match strategy, and she sounded steadier than she has in weeks. I have shortened Thursday's session by twenty minutes so she can sleep earlier before the test.
— Pradeep

qa.a: Due soon and matters long term.

qa.a: She sounded steadier and more in control than in weeks, after looking exhausted the week before.

qa.a: Pradeep backs it by shortening Thursday's session by twenty minutes so she can sleep earlier before the test.

passage:
Tuesday night
Three days to the Maths test, four to the district cricket final. Yash messaged at nine: "Online match tonight? Squad's on." I nearly said yes out of habit. Then I did what Coach says before a big over: stop and sort. Maths test: due soon, and it counts for the term. Final: due soon, and it's what I've trained all year for. Nets tomorrow: needed for the final. Gaming with the squad: fun, but neither urgent nor important, it'll be there next week. So gaming's out till Sunday. Nets stay. Maths gets an hour tonight and two tomorrow. Told Yash. He sent a crying emoji, then "fair, good luck in the final". Weird how saying no to one thing made the week feel smaller.
Vishal

qa.q: How many days were left before the Maths test?
How did Vishal feel after sorting the week?
qa.a: Vishal felt calmer and more in control; the week felt smaller once the gaming was dropped.

qa.q: Why keep nets instead of cutting sport too?
qa.a: The final is both urgent and important and nets feed straight into it, while gaming can wait a week without any cost.

qa.q: How does Yash react to Vishal's no?
qa.a: Yash is disappointed at first, sending a crying emoji, then understands and wishes Vishal luck in the final.
